chapter_title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation — ¶5

Know that the natural mind is like the ground of the external man, while the faculties and powers [GAP-1] of that mind are like perceptions. There are diverse kinds [GAP-2] of perception that one may find developing within the natural man. They arise and are renewed and become established. They have not [GAP-3] been destroyed beyond restoration. Again, there are other perceptions that, if they are struck down by falsity, shall not [GAP-4] be restored; yet others do regenerate, for they are li[GAP-5]ke those rooted perceptions that may be challenged yet spring forth again [GAP-6] and [GAP-7] — those also that arise [GAP-8] — they may be struck down and not regenerate, resembling [GAP-9] dead knowledges that neither regenerate nor shall they [GAP-10] bear any further use. It [sh]all be according to the Lord's will whether [GAP-11] a perception is renewed and grows [GAP-12]. But whatever develops in profanation [GAP-13] has its origin apart from Him. That corrupted selfhood — the will vitiated by hereditary evil — [GAP-14] dwells within the regenerating will, and those faculties [GAP-15] remain in a state of spiritual disorder.

---

**Translator's note on the governing correspondence:** The entire passage teaches that perceptions rooted in the natural mind vary as to whether they can survive temptation and be restored. Some perceptions, grounded in genuine good, regenerate even when assailed by falsity (trees that grow back when cut). Others, having no living root in charity, perish permanently when challenged. The closing lines introduce the deeper problem: corrupted selfhood (*proprium*) persists even within the regenerating will, producing a mixed and spiritually weakened state — what the text calls being "somewhat sick."

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Happen you know th[at the] body is like the earth, wh[ile these] limbs als[o and members] of it are like the trees. There are varieties [and kinds] of tree you shall find growing on the earth. They ar[is]e and grow again and stand firm. They have not [perished, for when they are cut they grow] Again, there are others that if they are cut shall not [grow again] and they grow, as they are li[ke the trees] which shall be cut and grow [again] and [stand firm] they too that occur [on the earth] they shall be cut and not grow, resembling [dead trees that neither] grow nor shall they [bear fruit upon the earth] it [sh]all please him on [the body] and grows [again] in impurity [it does not come] from him. This flesh that is corrupt [it is found and it dwells] in the liv[in]g flesh and they [that abide within it] are somewhat sick.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading gives "faculties and powers of that mind," which in the body-metaphor register becomes "limbs also and members" — a typical Kephalaia doubled expression for the body's constituent parts.
The spiritual reading says "diverse kinds of perception"; the Kephalaia frequently uses doubled synonyms ("varieties and kinds") to express completeness of classification.

fills.fill: perished, for when they are cut they grow
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "not destroyed beyond restoration," meaning these trees survive cutting — expressed in the tree metaphor as not perishing because they always grow back when cut.

The spiritual reading says "shall not be restored," which in the tree metaphor translates to "shall not grow again" — the visible "grow" in the manuscript is completed by "again" to express failed regeneration.

The spiritual reading gives "like those rooted perceptions"; in the natural register this becomes "like the trees," completing the partial word "li[ke the trees]" and maintaining the governing tree-body correspondence.
The spiritual reading says "spring forth again," and "again" directly completes "shall be cut and grow again" — echoing the identical phrase used earlier in the passage for resilient trees.

The spiritual reading completes the regeneration cycle at GAP-7; "stand firm" echoes the identical phrase used in the first category ("arise and grow again and stand firm"), expressing the full restoration of a perception after temptation.
The spiritual reading says "those also that arise [GAP-8]," locating them within the natural mind; in the governing correspondence (body = earth), this is expressed as "on the earth."
The spiritual reading says "resembling dead knowledges that neither regenerate"; in the tree metaphor, dead knowledges are "dead trees," and "neither" is already visible at the gap's end.
The spiritual reading says "bear any further use," which in the tree-on-earth metaphor becomes "bear fruit upon the earth" — dead trees produce nothing of spiritual use in the natural mind.

The spiritual reading says "whether a perception is renewed"; in the body/tree metaphor, the Lord's will determines what grows on "the body," maintaining the governing correspondence (body = natural mind).
The spiritual reading confirms a perception "is renewed and grows," and "again" naturally completes "grows again" — the standard phrase throughout this passage for regeneration after cutting.
The spiritual reading says "has its origin apart from Him"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, this becomes "it does not come from him" — what grows in impurity does not originate from the Lord.

fills.fill: it is found and it dwells
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says the corrupted selfhood "dwells within the regenerating will"; in the flesh metaphor, the corrupt flesh "is found and dwells" in the living flesh — expressing the co-presence of the proprium within the regenerating man.

The spiritual reading says "those faculties remain in a state of spiritual disorder"; the relative clause "that abide within it" identifies the limbs/faculties dwelling within the mixed body before the predicate "are somewhat sick."
